items.title: Supreme Court strikes down Karnataka law protecting tainted appointments, questions High Court ruling
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday struck down Karnataka Civil Services (Validation of Selection and Appointment of 2011 Batch Gazetted Probationers) Act, 2022, which validated around 191 appointments that had earlier been cancelled over allegations of corruption and nepotism [Srinavasa T v State of Karnataka and Others] A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran held that the 2022 law was unconstitutional, as the State legislature could not overturn the cancellation of these appointments after the decision had been upheld by constitutional courts. Having set aside the 2022 law, the Court ruled that the appointments made pursuant to the tainted recruitment "will also come to an end." “We have no doubt in our minds that the subject legislation is unconstitutional,” the Court ruled. The Court declined to order fresh recruitment to these posts under the old rules. Instead, it directed the Karnataka government to notify existing Group A and B vacancies under the current recruitment rules. items.title: Supreme Court to vet RBI’s digital fraud regulations before notification, says banks must compensate victims
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday said that it would examine the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI’s) proposed anti-cyber fraud regulations before they are notified. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing suo motu proceedings concerning digital arrest scams. The case arose from a senior citizen couple’s complaint of losing ₹1.05 crore to impersonators using forged judicial orders. It said that the regulations must require financial institutions to compensate victims where fraud results from failed due diligence. Compensation must be at least equivalent to the customer’s loss, the Court said. “The amount will remain intact. The bank will have to pay. That is the only way,” the CJI remarked, stressing that liability could not stop with individual officers. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana Justice Bagchi questioned why financial institutions should not face strict liability when their failure to provide safeguards enables misuse of banking products. items.title: NLUO announces Double Credit Course on Economics of Competition Law
items.summary: The Centre for Corporate Law, National Law University Odisha (NLUO), has announced a Double Credit Course on Economics of Competition Law , scheduled to be conducted online during November and December 2026. About the Course The course is designed to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of the economic principles and regulatory issues that govern competition law. It covers abuse of dominance, vertical restraints, cartels, mergers, and state aid, along with quantitative and empirical analysis, using practical examples and case studies. About the Resource Person Dr Nidhi Singh is an Advocate-on-Record (AoR) at the Supreme Court of India and practises across several US jurisdictions, including New York, New Jersey, California, Arizona, and Texas. With over a decade of litigation experience, her practice spans across constitutional law, service law, arbitration, antitrust, and financial regulation. She holds a JSM from Stanford Law School, an MSc in Law and Finance from the University of Oxford, and a postgraduate diploma in Economics for Competition Law from King's College London. items.title: The charity commissioner as kingmaker: Caveats, freezes and the battle for Tata Sons
items.summary: For most of its 76 years, the Maharashtra Public Trusts Act, 1950 has been the quiet statute of temple committees, school societies and hospital trusts. In 2026, it has become the principal battleground for control of India’s largest business group. The office of the Charity Commissioner in Worli has been receiving complaints and caveats in a volume that would be unusual even for a busy civil court. These come from the Tata Trusts, from their chairman and his son, and from dissenting trustees. Every party is racing to be heard first, or at least not to be heard last. This article traces how a forum designed to protect charitable property has ended up determining whether the holding company of that group can hold a valid annual general meeting. It then asks whether the law, as it stands, is equipped for that role. How we got here The immediate trigger was legislative. By an Ordinance promulgated on September 1, 2025 , since replaced by the Maharashtra Public Trusts (Second Amendment) Act, 2025 , the State inserted Section 30A into the 1950 Act. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday held that High Courts can order the restoration of electricity supply that was disconnected over disputed allegations of theft, but advised against adopting a liberal approach in such cases [ Dakshin Gujarat Vij Vs Vaibhav Crusher ]. A Bench of Justices Manoj Misra and KV Viswanathan observed that electricity is essential for life and livelihood, and that its deprivation could have serious consequences. items.title: Will Gen Z vote out the BJP in ‘27? Sreenivasan Jain asks UP’s youth
items.summary: For nearly three months, young people have been protesting in Delhi and other cities. Will these protests have an electoral impact? Sreenivasan Jain travels to Uttar Pradesh, which goes to the polls early next year, to find out what the state’s Gen Z is thinking. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP won almost 30 fewer seats in the state than it did in 2019. In Sultanpur, Jain meets students at a coaching centre who are preparing for government jobs. Garima Verma, 23, has been preparing for the civil services for three years. She is critical of the state’s education system. “Compare primary schools in Bombay and Delhi with our primary schools here. That’s how big the difference is at our basic level,” she says.She wants the government to work on education and employment, but says it isn't responding. “Gen Z asks questions and nobody answers them.” Muskan Sahu, 21, is a first-time voter. “Look at any exam: UP Police, Lekhpal, NTPC, CGL, whatever you like. items.title: Centre says tribal leaders are not ‘necessary’ parties to Great Nicobar forest rights dispute
items.summary: The Union Tribal Affairs Ministry has said that Nicobarese leaders seeking to join a petition challenging the settlement of forest rights on Great Nicobar Island are “neither necessary nor proper parties,” in the case, court documents show. The Nicobarese are one of two major tribes affected by the development of the Island, and primary claimants to forest rights in the area. An ongoing petition in the Calcutta High Court, filed by former IAS officer Meena Gupta, has challenged the Union government’s claim that rights under the Forest Rights Act (2005) (FRA) were settled on the Island. The FRA recognises the historical rights of tribal and other forest dwelling communities over forest resources, and makes compliance with its statutes necessary in clearing forest land for diversion. On July 9, 2026, four Nicobarese residents sought to join Gupta’s plea, arguing that government certifications claiming the settlement of forest rights was based on gram sabha consent from non-tribal settler communities. Cyclone Arnab battered parts of eastern Andhra Pradesh state Wednesday, killing three people, damaging homes and infrastructure and inundating roughly 200,000 acres of cropland, according to state authorities. Heavy rainfall was the biggest threat inland as the storm weakened. Meteorologists said unusually high temperatures across the Bay of Bengal helped fuel Arnab. Its arrival on a coastline where billions of dollars are being invested in data centers at early stages of construction underscored how extreme weather threatens both existing livelihoods and the infrastructure intended to drive future growth, climate experts said. It will likely take days or weeks for full damage estimates to be calculated. items.title: Dual PAN card case: Allahabad High Court grants bail to Azam Khan, refuses stay on conviction
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Thursday granted bail to Samajwadi Party leader Mohd Azam Khan and his son Abdullah Azam in the dual PAN card case [Mohd Azam Khan vs State of UP and 3 others]. Justice Samit Gopal suspended their sentences while their revision petitions challenging their conviction are pending. The Court observed that Khan and his son had already served substantial portions of their fixed-term sentences. "Looking to the nature of occurrence, period of detention of the accused/revisionists, the fact that the case in hand is for a fixed term of sentence, the present case is a fit case where the accused/revisionists... be enlarged on bail," the Court said. Justice Samit Gopal The case stems from a 2019 complaint by BJP leader Akash Saxena alleging that Abdullah Azam Khan in a planned conspiracy with his father procured a second PAN card with a forged date of birth to bypass age criteria to fraudulently contest the 2017 Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls from Rampur's Suar constituency.
